question: A non-stress test (NST) is performed at 34 weeks gestation. The trace shows no fetal heart rate accelerations over a 40-minute period. Which statement best describes this finding?

answers.text: It is reassuring because absence of accelerations in the third trimester is normal.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is incorrect. In the third trimester, at least 2 accelerations of ≥15 bpm lasting ≥15 seconds in a 20-minute window are required for a reactive NST.

answers.text: It is non-reactive and requires further evaluation, such as a biophysical profile.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A non-reactive NST (no accelerations in 40 minutes) is an indication for further evaluation. A biophysical profile (BPP) is the standard next step.

answers.text: It confirms fetal compromise and immediate delivery is indicated.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A non-reactive NST alone does not mandate immediate delivery — it triggers further evaluation (BPP). Only a BPP score ≤4 with oligohydramnios would prompt urgent delivery.

answers.text: It is acceptable because fetal sleep cycles can last up to 60 minutes.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Fetal sleep cycles last 20–40 minutes, not 60 minutes. The standard protocol extends monitoring to 40 minutes before classifying as non-reactive.

overallFeedback.feedback: A non-reactive NST is defined as fewer than 2 accelerations in 40 minutes. The next step is a biophysical profile, not immediate delivery.
Well done. Non-reactive NST → biophysical profile is the standard escalation pathway in fetal surveillance.
